input:
Integral 1/[sin(x-a) sin x] dx =

Options:
A. sin(a) log(sin(x-a)cosec x) + c
B. cosec(a) log(sin(x-a)cosec x) + c
C. -sin(a) log(sin(x-a)sin x) + c
D. -cosec(a) log(sin(x-a)sin x) + c

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Evaluate the integral involving product of two sine factors in denominator.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Use identity sin x - sin(x-a) = 2cos((2x-a)/2)sin(a/2), or direct decomposition using cot terms.

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Rewrite integrand as difference of cotangents, then integrate termwise.

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: Differentiation returns csc(a)[cot(x-a)-cot x] which equals the original integrand.
